subject: Post-call: Residency & Isolation constraints — MedSure discovery (recap & next steps)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Ramirez <alex.ramirez@medsure.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Sep 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Residency & Isolation constraints — MedSure discovery (recap & next steps)

Alex — thanks for the time today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we don’t lose momentum. I tried to keep this tight; please correct anything I’ve misunderstood.

Key pain points you shared
- Primary: must ensure all PHI processing occurs in an environment that is physically isolated from the public internet (air-gap or equivalent controls).
- Network: only outbound egress via an approved bastion/proxy; strict CIDR allowlist and no public load-balancers in front of model hosts.
- Compliance: evidence of key controls (SOC 2, encryption at rest & in transit, KMS/HSM) required for internal review and board sign-off.

Primary goals
1) Run inference on customer-controlled infrastructure (on-prem or VPC with dedicated connectivity) so model inputs/outputs never traverse Redwood-hosted public endpoints.
2) Keep latency under 250ms p50 for critical inference paths.
3) Maintain auditable logs and retention policy (90 days initial ask; will confirm).

Constraints / open technical unknowns (items we need from you)
- Exact CIDR ranges and outbound proxy/bastion details (required for routing/NSG design)
- Whether MedSure will accept a VPC deployment reachable only via ExpressRoute/DirectConnect, or must be fully air-gapped with physical media transport for model updates.
- Confirmation of required key management — do you require HSM-backed keys (FIPS 140-2) on day one?

What Redwood can offer (initial proposal)
- Redwood Private deployed into MedSure VPC with strict network policy, optional private link endpoints, and no public-facing ELBs.
- HSM/KMS integration for model encryption and API auth; audit logging exported to your SIEM.
- A 90-minute technical deep-dive to walk your infra and security teams through topology, failover, and patch/update procedures.

Proposed next steps (please pick owners and timelines)
- Alex / MedSure SecOps: share network topology + CIDR allowlist and list of approved egress proxies (owner: Alex) — target: 2028-09-18.
- Marissa (me): schedule technical deep-dive with Redwood infra + devops — propose 2028-09-19 or 20 (two 60–90 min slots).
- Priyom: prepare concise SOW options (on-prem appliance vs VPC private deployment) and a high-level cost delta.
- Ben: draft initial procurement checklist for your procurement team (data flow, SLA, support coverage).

Attachments: redwood-hosting-brief.pdf (light brief on deployment options and controls).

If this aligns, Alex — I’ll send a calendar invite for the deep-dive once you confirm availability for 9/19 or 9/20.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions Lead
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Alex Ramirez <alex.ramirez@medsure.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, security@medsure.com
Date: Tue, 12 Sep 2028 17:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Residency & Isolation constraints — MedSure discovery (recap & next steps)

Thanks for the clear recap — spot on. A few clarifications from SecOps and infra that will affect architecture: 

Operational constraints (MedSure)
- All PHI processing must be isolated from the internet. Prefer an on-prem cluster; acceptable alternative is a VPC with dedicated private connectivity (ExpressRoute) and zero public egress.
- Our outbound policy: only the approved bastion (10.10.0.5) can connect out; no direct internet access from GPU hosts. Updates to models must be pushed via an internal update server or physical media.
- CIDR allowlist: 10.10.0.0/16 for internal services; 172.20.100.0/24 reserved for bastion/proxy. We will provide full diagram.

Compliance asks
- HSM-backed KMS required for production keys. We also need an attestation that Redwood can operate with FIPS-validated modules.
- Audit log retention: 365 days preferred, but we can accept 90 days for initial PoC.

Attachments: medsure-topology-v1.drawio.png (network sketch).

Available for the deep-dive 9/19 10:00–11:30 PT or 9/20 14:00–15:30 PT. I can bring our infra lead (Jin Park) and SecOps.

Alex Ramirez
Director, Infrastructure
MedSure Health
alex.ramirez@medsure.com
(650) 555-0147

Appreciate the detail, Alex. Two quick clarifying items from our side so we can size and propose properly: 

1) Model update cadence: do you expect weekly model updates pushed by MedSure or quarterly updates from Redwood (we can support both; the update method affects the operational approach for an air-gapped option).
2) Failover expectations: if the primary on-prem cluster becomes unavailable, do you want an active-standby in another datacenter (still private) or manual restore?

Action: Priyom / I will draft 2 path options in the SOW — (A) VPC + ExpressRoute with private endpoints and HSM; (B) Fully on-prem appliance with physical update workflow. We'll note the cost/time delta. Expect a draft by 2028-09-18.

—Ben
